transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Northstar Eng Manager), Ethan Chen (Backend), Priya Shah (Security)

00:00 Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll keep this fairly focused — SDK quickstart and auth setup for Northstar. Quick roll call?
00:12 Maya Lopez: Maya here, hi.
00:14 Ethan Chen: Ethan, hi.
00:16 Priya Shah: Priya here.
00:18 Jordan Park: Great. Samira, Liam, you wanna quick intro?
00:21 Samira Khan: Yeah hi I'm Samira, Solutions Engineer on Redwood, I usually run the SDK walkthroughs and integration patterns.
00:27 Liam Ortiz: Liam, I work on the console and billing side so I can cover quotas and pilot config.
00:31 Jordan Park: Awesome. So agenda, show Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth patterns, environment setup, then a short Console demo and some Optimize recommendations, and leave time for Q&A.

02:05 Samira Khan: Okay opening the shared screen — here's the repo, "redwood-quickstarts/sdk". In Python we have two files: quickstart.py and streaming_example.py. In TypeScript it's index.ts and examples/client.ts.
02:23 Ethan Chen: How long before we can call it from our backend? We run Go services but we can put a small node shim.
02:30 Samira Khan: Totally. For a minimal test you only need to set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_BASE_URL env vars, pip install redwood-sdk, then run quickstart. The Python snippet: import redwood; client = redwood.Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))...
02:58 Maya Lopez: Are those environment variables the recommended way, or do you recommend SSO for prod?
03:05 Samira Khan: Environment vars are simplest for dev. For prod we support SSO + OAuth flows for the Console plus scoped API tokens. We can also do rotating service credentials via your vault and KMS. If you have a private deployment we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key wrapping.

05:10 Jordan Park: Quick note on auth patterns — many customers start with API keys for the pilot, then move to short-lived tokens and automated rotation. Priya, is there a specific compliance bar you need to meet?
05:22 Priya Shah: SOC 2 controls around key management, audit logs, and SAML SSO for admin access. Also we need the option to keep logs in our VPC.
05:31 Liam Ortiz: For audit logs we can push logs to your SIEM or S3; Console retention is configurable. For VPC/private we have Redwood Private options — control plane can be customer-managed and we support KMS integrations.

07:00 Samira Khan: Back to SDK — demoing the TypeScript client now. npm i @redwood/sdk, set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, then const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_BASE_URL }); client.generate({model: 'redwood/gpt-4o-mini', prompt: 'Hello'}).then(...).
07:40 Ethan Chen: That model name — will my traffic hit hosted endpoints or can we pin to a Dedicated pool?
07:48 Samira Khan: You can choose. For pilot you can use hosted catalog. For higher throughput or guaranteed SLOs you'd move to Dedicated — in the SDK you pass a route or model id and for internal routing we honor the routing policies.

09:12 Maya Lopez: Any gotchas around connection reuse for Node? We're concerned about the token overhead per request.
09:20 Samira Khan: We support persistent client instances and HTTP/2 keepalive. Also recommend batching for high throughput — Redwood Optimize gives suggestions on batch size and quantization profiles.

11:05 Priya Shah: On encryption — do you store customer data? What's redwood's retention?
11:12 Jordan Park: Hosted has configurable retention; default is 30 days for request logs but we can turn off retention. For Private deployments the data stays in your network; we can integrate with your KMS. I'll attach the SOC2 and security pack after the call.

12:40 Samira Khan: Showing quickstart.py live: the call demonstrates synchronous generate and a streaming example. Note that streaming uses a websocket or SSE endpoint depending on your client; Python uses the async client.
12:58 Ethan Chen: Is streaming supported in TypeScript easily?
13:02 Samira Khan: Yes, client.stream() returns an async iterator; but watch out for chunking behavior — sometimes transcript tokens arrive fragmented, the SDK includes a helper to stitch partial deltas.

15:30 Jordan Park: We often see transcription issues when people paste logs; small note, the console displays token cost estimates per request. Liam do you wanna show the console quick route creation?
15:42 Liam Ortiz: Sure — here's the Console. You can create an API route, pin a model, set quotas and a dedicated pool if you have Dedicated. For pilot we'll set a route to the hosted endpoint but lock to a specific model family.

17:10 Maya Lopez: How do we test latency? We care about 95th p95 under 200ms for short prompts.
17:18 Samira Khan: For short prompts and smaller models that's achievable on Dedicated GPUs with right batching config. For hosted we have performance profiles; we can run a benchmark on sample payloads and return a latency/cost sheet. That would be part of the pilot.

19:00 Ethan Chen: About Quantization — you mentioned Optimize recommendations — how much custom work is that going to be on our side?
19:08 Samira Khan: Optimize suggests quant profiles based on your sequence lengths and payload distribution. Minimal engineering: enable a recommended profile and run your validation prompts to check quality. We can also run a quantization trial in our staging and share the validation reports.

21:35 Priya Shah: Network security — if we use Redwood Private, can we do egress restrictions and use our own NAT?
21:44 Liam Ortiz: Yes, Private deployments live in your VPC and you control egress and peering. We can provide a deployment manifest and work with your infra team.

23:00 Samira Khan: Back to code, quick auth examples for SSO: admins authenticate via SAML/SSO in the Console; for service-to-service, you can mint short-lived tokens via an OAuth flow or via our token rotation API tied to your vault. Example: POST /v1/tokens with client_assertion... we also provide a helm chart for on-prem.

25:20 Ethan Chen: Is there an SDK call to rotate keys automatically or do we need to script that?
25:28 Samira Khan: We have a token rotate endpoint and a small rotation helper in the SDK; you can plug it into your existing vault job.

27:40 Maya Lopez: Let's walk through a quick end-to-end dev flow — Samira?
27:46 Samira Khan: Sure: 1) Create Console route and generate a scoped API token; 2) Create a service user in your vault and store the token; 3) In dev set REDWOOD_API_KEY locally and run quickstart; 4) Run the benchmark script in repo to capture latency; 5) Iterate on batch size recommended by Optimize.

30:00 Jordan Park: I'll note the pilot scope: 2 weeks, 3 endpoints, sample dataset of anonymized transactions, run latency and cost benchmarks, Security review with Priya.
30:20 Priya Shah: We'll need an NDA and the SOC2 docs before we share any sample data.
30:27 Jordan Park: Understood — I'll attach the NDA and security pack.

32:10 Samira Khan: Quick note about permissions — Console uses RBAC, you can restrict routes to teams and set viewer/admin roles. We log actions for audit trails.

33:50 Ethan Chen: For our Go stack, any examples for direct API calls from Go?
33:58 Samira Khan: Not in the quickstart repo but we have a community example; it's a simple HTTP POST with Authorization: Bearer <token>. I can paste a minimal Go snippet in the notes.

36:00 Maya Lopez: What's the typical ramp from pilot to Dedicated?
36:06 Jordan Park: Usually after a successful pilot we discuss committed capacity and expected QPS. Dedicated contracts often start monthly with reserved GPUs and predictable SLOs. We can do burst capacity as well.

38:15 Priya Shah: Any data residency options in EU? We have EU customers.
38:22 Liam Ortiz: Yes, region pinning is supported and Private can be deployed in EU regions; hosted catalog also has region-specific endpoints. We'll include region availability in the follow-up.

40:00 Samira Khan: Quick demo of the Optimize tab — it surfaced a suggestion to reduce batch size for lower tail latency and to enable prefix caching for common prompts, and it suggested a quant profile for the 8-bit trial.

42:30 Ethan Chen: If we enable prefix caching will that store any PII? We prefer to avoid caching sensitive fields.
42:40 Samira Khan: You can configure caching rules; we typically recommend stripping PII before caching and we support opt-out. For Private, caching can be confined to your infra.

44:10 Jordan Park: Alright let's do a short recap and next steps.
44:15 Jordan Park: Next steps — I'll send the security pack, NDA, and pricing. Samira will drop the code samples and a short recording. We'll schedule the pilot kickoff week of Mar 22 pending NDA.
44:29 Maya Lopez: That sounds good.
44:31 Priya Shah: Thank you.
44:33 Ethan Chen: Thanks all.
44:35 Jordan Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
45:00 End of recording.
